label: Earlier states are causal ancestors of populated states
definition: PrecedenceIsStateCausation h Concrete stateCause w holds when, in every history v accessible from w, whenever a contingent concrete individual is present at moment t and s is strictly earlier than t, there is a chain of one or more stateCause v edges from s to t. In ordinary language: the state of a possible history at any earlier moment lies in the causal history of its state at each moment where a contingent thing is present.
note: Explicit analyst bridge from mere temporal precedence to causation; attribution deferred. It is the step an endless past of mere succession need not take: a history whose earlier states are causally idle with respect to later ones rejects it. It is the strong, global form (every earlier moment, not only some); it is restricted to populated later moments. Applicability OPEN.
